byte_accounting_notes.basis: same four-axis basis as receipts/cross-candidate-byte-accounting.json (file bytes / tensor bytes / transformer body / deployed multimodal); body = payload minus embedding, head, vision tower and MTP draft. Computed from safetensors headers: local digest-verified snapshots for the turbo rungs, HTTP Range reads at the pinned revisions for saka and awq (tensor payloads never re-downloaded).
observations_no_fidelity_claims: turbo6's transformer body is 17.0537 GiB -- byte-identical to the K6-parity build's predicted body (receipts/preregistration-kld9-window.json k6_parity_predicted_body_gib 17.0537) and within 0.02 GiB of GGUF UD-Q5_K_XL's 17.034: the uniform 6.00bpw rung is a natural BODY-parity comparator for the K6-parity build, not just a file-parity one.

turbo5's body is 14.2217 GiB against the context edition's 14.8858: the 5.00bpw control carries 0.664 GiB LESS body than our nearest build, so on the body axis the ctx pairing reads in the control's favour before any KLD is measured -- the paired sentence must name its axis.

turbo5/turbo6 share byte-identical embedding (BF16 2.3682), head (exl3 K6 0.8885), vision (BF16 0.8582) and MTP (exl3-4bit 0.198): the two rungs differ ONLY in body bytes, which is exactly what a uniform-bitrate control should do.

saka and awq both ship BF16 head (2.3682) and BF16 MTP (0.7911); saka's body is 12.7614 GiB, awq's 13.1887 -- the two community 4-bit artifacts spend ~1.5 GiB of their envelope on an unquantized head where every EXL3/GGUF comparator quantizes it.
